Items.Authors: Rima Islam, Aline Dinkelaker, Abani Shankar Nayak, Kalaga V. Madhav, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: Commissioning the AIP's ultrafast laser-inscription facility: defining the parameter space for type-I waveguide fabrication
Items.Abstract: This work details the iterative statistical optimization of the femtosecond-based ultrafast laser inscription system—specifically pulse energy, repetition rate, translation speed, and scan density to achieve Type-1 positive refractive-index modifications. We present the resulting fabrication recipe for single-mode, high-throughput waveguides optimized for the astronomical J-band (1300-1400 nm). By achieving precise Mode Field Diameter (MFD) matching with standard optical fibers, we ensure low insertion loss. The optimization of parameter space is critical for the fabrication of complex devices, such as photonic reformatters, beam combiners, and pupil remappers, for future deployment at the CHARA array and Calar Alto Observatory.

Items.Authors: M. Viveganandam, J. Adassuriya, K. P. S. C. Jayaratne
Items.Title: Compact medium-resolution spectrograph for alt-azimuth mounted Cassegrain telescopes: optical design and performance analysis
Items.Abstract: Alt-azimuth mounted telescopes with Cassegrain focus offer affordability and versatility but often lack the clearance needed to attach standard commercial spectrographs. To overcome this limitation, we developed a compact, cost-effective, medium-resolution spectrograph specifically designed for seamless integration with such telescopes. The instrument incorporates a 1200 grooves/mm diffraction grating and a narrow slit aperture, with optical performance evaluated using Zemax OpticStudio 2025 R2 ray-tracing simulations. Results confirm effective spectral dispersion, accurate focusing of RGB wavelengths, and strong agreement with theoretical expectations. Aberration analysis shows negligible higher-order effects, with only slight spherical aberration present. Overall, the spectrograph demonstrates excellent image quality and validates a practical, accessible solution for high-resolution astronomical spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Alikhan Basheer, Devika Divakar, Pramod Panchal, Sanjeev Jha, Prasanna Deshmukh, Sudarsan Kambhala, Karthic Kumar, Sriram Sripadmanabhan
Items.Title: Comparative study of roundel support system for sub aperture metrology of segmented telescope mirrors
Items.Abstract: As a partner of the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) project, India has agreed to supply 84 polished segments for the primary mirror, using the innovative Stressed Mirror Polishing (SMP) technology obtained from Coherent Inc., USA. Some of the metrology tools for the SMP process are designed and developed by India TMT (ITMT) team such as the 27-point whiffletree-based support system. This system acts as the support structure during the entire metrology activities of polished TMT Roundel.   The study focuses on a comparative analysis of Roundel Support systems used in one of the metrology processes, which is Sub Aperture Metrology to capture the Band 2-6 data. It contrasts results from the 43-point hydraulic-based support system at Coherent with the 27-point whiffletree-based support system developed by I-TMT. This analysis assesses efficacy and performance differences between the two support systems, involving a comprehensive examination of a 1520mm diameter polished glass roundel.

Items.Authors: Reuben Neate, Tinus Stander
Items.Title: Concept design of a single-IC integrated 183GHz direct detection water vapour radiometer
Items.Abstract: The requirements for an 183 GHz water vapour radiometer (WVR) are considered, and design specifications are proposed. The proposed design is found to be achievable through single-IC integration of a radiometer using a 165 GHz direct detection receiver, consisting of a calibration switch with controllable thermal load, low noise amplifier (LNA), and power detector. The design is found to produce a compact, lightweight WVR, suitable for integration in confined spaces. The single-IC integration also lends itself to arrayed receiver design, of which a concept is presented.

Items.Authors: Johan Kosmalski, Luca Pasquini
Items.Title: Concepts for a large field corrector and atmospheric dispersion compensator for the Nasmyth focus of the Very Large Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Nasmyth foci of the four VLT 8m telescopes at paranal Observatory offer the largest Field of View available for Multi-Object-Spectrographs (MOS). Given the several interface restrictions present, so far none of these foci has been equipped with an Atmospheric Dispersion Compensator (ADC), that, on the other hand, could be highly beneficial for MOS observations over a large wavelength range. In this work we present two new optical concepts that provide a full Nasmyth corrected field, that respect the VLT interface prescription.

Items.Authors: Zhuo-Xiao Wang, Song Huang, Gang Ji, Tian-Yang Hu, Zhong-Tian Tian, Wei Qin, Li-Quan Guo, Run-Dong Fan, Jun-Sen Lao, Pei Li, Meng-Fan He, Cheng Zhao, Lei Huang, Zheng Cai, Diane C. Kerouanton, Malak Galal, Gloria Mellinand, Sébastien Pernecker, Maxime Rombach, Oliver P. Suárez, Eirini Tagkoudi, Jonathan Wei, Jean-Paul Kneib, Johannes Wuethrich, Guandi Zhao, Marcelle Soares-Santos
Items.Title: Conceptual design for the focal plane system of the 6.5-m multiplexed survey telescope for stage-V cosmological surveys
Items.Abstract: MUltiplexed Survey Telescope (MUST) is a 6.5m telescope dedicated to wide-field spectroscopic surveys in the 2030s, motivated by Stage-V cosmology requirements. Under construction in China, MUST hosts ~20,000 6.2-mm-pitch fiber-positioning robots on a 1.2m diameter, aspheric, highly modular focal-plane system, enabling unprecedented multiplexing over a ~6 deg² field of view. We present the conceptual design and performance estimates of MUST's focal plane system. As EPFL is developing MUST's fiber positioning module (FPM) and will report its progress separately, we focus on the scientific requirements, key engineering challenges, and implementation plan for the focal plane system led by the Tsinghua team. In particular, we will present the current plan to meet the challenging fiber defocus and tilt tolerance budget, discuss integration with MUST's active optics and the in-situ metrology system for FPM maintenance, and share lessons learned for next-generation spectroscopic facilities.

Items.Authors: Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, René Laporte, Claudia Lúcia Mendes de Oliveira, Alex Cavaliéri Carciofi, Antonio Nazareno Uchoa de Oliveira Filho, André Gasparotto Pelosi, Júlia Akiyama da Silva, Ariane Cristina Fonseca Silva, Tommy Lazaneo Zirnberger
Items.Title: Conceptual design of a dual-arm imager with polarimetric capability for the T80-S telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the conceptual development of a new dual-arm imaging instrument for the T80-South telescope, designed to extend the capabilities by combining broad- and narrow-band imaging with linear and circular polarimetry. The system splits the incoming beam into two optical channels optimized for complementary spectral coverage, enabling simultaneous acquisition. A polarization modulator and a dual-beam analyzer provide differential measurements of orthogonal linear polarization states. The polarimetric subsystem is being optimized for moderate-precision measurements of bright sources, maintaining a larger field of view than conventional narrow-field polarimeters. Scientific goals include wide-area mapping of interstellar polarization, characterization of circumstellar density and geometry of several classes of stellar objects, and narrowband polarimetric studies of emission-line structures.

Items.Authors: Naoshi Murakami, Shunya Sato, Kenta Yoneta, Jun Nishikawa, Keigo Enya, Hajime Kawahara, Takayuki Kotani, Shota Miyazaki, Aoi Takahashi, Toru Yamada
Items.Title: Conceptual study of auxiliary optical module for multi-band high-contrast wavefront control
Items.Abstract: We performed numerical simulations to validate an auxiliary optical module proposed for enhancing the multi-band capability of wavefront control. The basic concept of this method is to provide differential field rotations for images in multiple spectral bands so that DM control modes are not superposed between the bands. We expect this technology to enable planetary surface mapping via multi-band photometric variations, as well as efficient spectral characterization of exoplanets over a broad wavelength range. Although the simulations are simplified and preliminary, the results suggest that contrasts at the 1E−10 level may be achievable simultaneously and independently across multiple spectral bands separated by approximately 30% in wavelength.

Items.Authors: Paweł Rukat
Items.Title: Construction of a laboratory model of an adaptive optics module for an amateur telescope
Items.Abstract: A numerical model of a hybrid adaptive optics system combining a deformable mirror (DM) and a liquid-crystal spatial light modulator (SLM) for astronomical observations is presented. The model includes atmospheric turbulence generation, Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensing, deformable mirror correction, SLM-based residual wavefront compensation, and image quality evaluation. Simulations show that hybrid correction extends diffraction-limited operation from a normalized actuator spacing of rs/r0 < 0.4 for a DM alone to rs/r0 < 1.7 with an SLM, reducing the required number of deformable mirror actuators by up to 90%. The temporal performance of the hybrid system is found to be primarily limited by the SLM refresh rate and depends on atmospheric wind velocity and normalized actuator spacing. A temporal stability map is presented to define the operating conditions under which diffraction-limited performance can be maintained.

Items.Authors: Davide Deiana, Guido Vecchia
Items.Title: Construction status of ESO ELT - DMS
Items.Abstract: The telescope Main Structure and the Dome of the ELT are being procured by ESO as an integrated system together with the auxiliary building and the service plants and are supplied by the ACe Consortium. The contract was signed in May 2016 and the path to final delivery has proven to be challenged by intricate, multi-faceted technical roadblocks emerging from every discipline.  The progress is visible and tangible; the primary and secondary structures are complete, and we are nearing completion of the physical installations (e.g. electrical, and fluid distribution), with commissioning just starting. However, there are various challenges yet to be overcome. In this paper we will describe the progress and achievements of the site construction so far as well as give an outline of the challenges involved in maintaining quality, productivity, and spirits high when building a giant telescope in the middle of the desert at 3000 m asl.

Items.Authors: Awatif Hiti, Gabriel Toshiaki Tayama, Simon Thibault
Items.Title: Contactless magnetorheological PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane) membrane for high-stroke deformable mirror
Items.Abstract: We present a contactless deformable mirror based on a PDMS membrane embedded with magnetite nanoparticles and actuated by a 37-magnet array. The 50 mm-diameter, 275 µm-thick membrane achieved deformations up to 0.97 mm under magnetic fields of 21–77 mT, with surface roughness between 3 and 7 nm. Experimental measurements and COMSOL simulations showed excellent agreement, confirming the potential of magnetic actuation to overcome the spatial limitations of conventional mirrors. This approach enables high-stroke, optical-quality deformation for adaptive optics applications in astronomy, laser communications, and vision science.

Items.Authors: Thomas Birbacher, Julio Pino Jiménez, Jonah T. Hansen, Germain Garreau, Adrian M. Glauser, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Control and compensation mechanisms for broadband nulling
Items.Abstract: Deep broadband cryogenic nulling is a prerequisite for the LIFE space mission to characterize habitable-zone exoplanets. While the top-level requirements on Optical Path Difference (OPD) and intensity mismatch are theoretically defined, achieving them across the 4 to 18.5 µm bandpass under cryogenic conditions remains an unresolved engineering challenge. Even sub-arcsecond errors in alignment or coating mismatches at the sub-percent level may be critical at the required nulls.    To prepare for the Nulling Interferometry Cryogenic Experiment (NICE), we present potential frameworks for the control and compensation of quasi-static chromatic, polarization, and alignment errors. Our reference strategy involves a careful static alignment and pre-compensation for cooling down, and to use targeted individual mechanisms. An alternative approach is the adaptive nuller. We compare the two and evaluate their suitability for a high-sensitivity, deep-contrast cryogenic nulling interferometer.

Items.Authors: Mingyeong Yang, Sang-Hyun Chun, Yongmin Yoon, Dongkok Kim, Yunjong Kim, Yongseok Lee, Sungwook E. Hong, Minhee Hyun, Jae-Woo Kim, Ho Seong Hwang, Hyeonguk Bahk, Young-Man Choi, Moo-Young Chun, Haeun Chung, Kim Dachan, Donghui Jeong, Kang-Min Kim, Jongwan Ko, Minseong Kwon, Ho-Gyu Lee, Jong Chul Lee, Chung-Uk Lee, Hyunho Lim, Heeyoung Oh, Changbom Park, Hyunmi Song
Items.Title: Control software development for A/K-SPEC: guiding, focusing, acquisition, and atmospheric dispersion correction systems
Items.Abstract: The All-Sky Spectroscopic Survey (A-SPEC) is an all-sky, large-volume, multi-object spectroscopic survey targeting galaxies with K_s < 13.75. The K-SPEC instrument system, developed for A-SPEC, is designed to deliver precise and efficient spectroscopic observations. This paper presents the design and implementation of the control software for the K-SPEC GFA (Guiding, Focusing, and Acquisition) and ADC (Atmospheric Dispersion Correction) systems. The software automates key observational procedures, providing both low-level device control and system monitoring. The K-SPEC GFA control system provides three core functions: simultaneous control of multiple guide cameras, acquisition of images from these cameras, and computation of guiding offsets from the acquired images. The K-SPEC ADC control system compensates for atmospheric dispersion by dynamically adjusting two prism motors in response to telescope pointing information.

Items.Authors: José Leonardo Garcés Medina, Enrique Colorado, Ximena Zepeda, Itzel Gonzalez-Ochoa, Jorge Fuentes-Fernández, Jaime Ruiz-Diaz, Fernando Ángeles, Alejandro Farah, Sebastián Sánchez
Items.Title: Control system design and implementation for EBANO, a low-cost scanning spectrograph at the OAN San Pedro Mártir
Items.Abstract: EBANO is a low-cost scanning spectrograph for the 84-cm telescope at San Pedro Mártir. Its control system integrates an EMCCD detector, a linear stage, and two custom COTS-based rotary stages that provide the fine angular motion required for wavelength scanning. EBANO is the first instrument designed under the observatory’s new client–server architecture, featuring a Python-based API for configuration, sequencing, monitoring, and network-based image transfer. The system includes an isolated local engineering interface and a robust software environment tolerant to unexpected power losses. This work summarizes the architecture, implementation, and current status of the EBANO control system, which will serve as a template for future OAN-SPM instruments.

Items.Authors: Hao A. Li, Jialin Pan, Qishuai Lu, Shouwei Hu
Items.Title: Cooperative control of a dual-stage compliant actuator for high-precision positioning
Items.Abstract: To address the trade-off between large stroke and nanometer resolution, this paper proposes a cooperative control strategy for a dual-stage compliant actuator. The system integrates a long-stroke coarse stage with a high-bandwidth compliant fine stage. Addressing inter-stage coupling and friction, a master-slave architecture featuring Zynq SoC dual-core parallel processing is designed. A robust controller compensates for fine-stage hysteresis, while the SoC allocates low-frequency signals to the coarse stage and high-frequency errors to the fine stage in real-time. Experimental results demonstrate the system achieves a 4 mm travel range, 5 nm positioning accuracy, and a 500 ms settling time. This provides an effective solution for segmented mirror active optics control.

Items.Authors: Isabella Castel-branco, Michael J. Freyberg
Items.Title: Correlating high-energy background between SRG/eROSITA and XMM-Newton/EPIC in the magnetosphere
Items.Abstract: Space-based X-ray imaging is hindered by background noise, which   principally originates from solar wind, coronal mass ejections and Galactic   Cosmic Rays. Whilst noise is inevitable, understanding it allows for   optimised mitigation. Our project aims to characterise the high energy space   environment by correlating the background enhancements detected between   XMM-Newton and SRG/eROSITA, wherein we explicitly compare their respective   environments -- near-Earth and L2 -- by studying individual solar particle   clouds' propagation. Enhancements at L2 were detected by eROSITA and sorted   using a statistical algorithm: these will then be cross-correlated with   XMM-Newton's near-Earth detections, with delays ranging from a few seconds for   relativistic particles and an hour for soft-proton clouds.   Spatially characterising the differentiated high-energy background environment   is essential to appropriately plan for future X-ray space observatories, such as the   upcoming NewAthena mission.

Items.Authors: A. K. Vaskuri, H. Agarwal, J. D. Wheeler, J. E. Austermann, S. M. Duff, M. R. Vissers, J. Hubmayr, J. Ullom
Items.Title: Cryogenic polarization response measurement system for long wavelength polarimetric detectors
Items.Abstract: We have developed a cryogenic polarization response measurement system based on a cryogenic stepper motor mounted on the 4 K stage used to characterize sub-Kelvin millimeter-wave polarization-sensitive detectors. The motor rotates an electrically-modulated cryogenic thinfilm blackbody source, Winston cone mirror, and custom-microfabricated wire-grid polarizer. In this work, the system is used to characterize the polarization response of sub-Kelvin polarimetric detectors across various spectral bands from 150 GHz to 850 GHz. When rotating the polarized source for a full revolution, one should see a detector response with two full periods of a sine wave, where the minimum is defined as the cross-polarization. We will present the polarization response measurements, compare the measured cross-polarization results against the simulations, provide breakout of the cross-polarization contributions, and estimate the corresponding combined expanded measurement uncertainty.

Items.Authors: Bruno V. Castilho, Márcio V. Vital de Arruda, Orlando Verducci, Jesulino B. dos Santos, Leandro H. dos Santos, Josimar A. Rosa, Clemens D. Gneiding, Beatriz S. Barbuy, Matteo Z. Genoni, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino, Igor Coretti
Items.Title: CUBES, the Cassegrain U-band efficient spectrograph: the calibration unit for the UV
Items.Abstract: The Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) for the ESO VLT is optimized for high-efficiency spectroscopy in the near-UV (300–405 nm) at R > 20,000 (and R ~ 7,000 in a lower-resolution mode). Achieving accurate calibration in this spectral region poses specific challenges, including the scarcity of suitable continuum and line sources and stringent stability requirements for flat-fielding and wavelength calibration. We present the final design of the CUBES Calibration Unit, which passed its Final Design Review in July 2025 and is now in the MAIT phase. The system provides flat-field, wavelength calibration, and illumination characterization through a dedicated optical path feeding the instrument at the Cassegrain focus. We describe the calibration strategy, the optical and mechanical architecture, the control electronics, and performance predictions. Installation at the VLT is planned for 2030.

Items.Authors: Julian Stürmer, Christopher Ritz, Carmen Feiz, Edoardo Redaelli, Stephen Watson, Joel Harman, Matteo Genoni, Walter Seifert, Lawrence Bissell, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio M. Pariani, Hans Dekker, Chris Waring, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino, Stefano Cristiani, Andreas Quirrenbach
Items.Title: CUBES: mechanical design and analysis for high-resolution UV spectroscopy on the VLT
Items.Abstract: The Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) is a next-generation, high-resolution UV spectrograph for the Very Large Telescope (VLT), covering 300-405nm with R > 20000. We present the mechanical design and opto-mechanical analysis, including challenges and constraints that impacted the system layout and material choices. Finite Element Analysis verifies compliance with ESO standards. To mitigate variable gravity loads, we developed an active flexure compensation system to maximize optical performance.

Items.Authors: Lawrence Bissell, Walter Seifert, Ariadna Calcines Rosario, Gerardo Avila, Hans Dekker, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Genoni, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino
Items.Title: CUBES: optical design and analysis of the VLT’s high-resolution UV spectrograph past final design review
Items.Abstract: CUBES (Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph) will be the most efficient UV spectrograph on an 8-10m telescope, exploiting the ESO VLT’s higher telescope efficiency relative to the ESO ELT in ground-based UV wavelengths. The instrument provides wavelength coverage over a range of 300-405nm, with high instrumental efficiency (>37%) and a resolving power of >20,000 (HR) and >6,000 (LR). This paper presents the finalised optical design and analysis of the system after the final design review. The optical subsystems detailed include: a pair of UV-optimized atmospheric dispersion correctors designed to function out to a zenith angle of 65°; high throughput HR and LR image slicers used to reformat the field-of-view; and a non-axisymmetric three-lens spectrograph camera design.

Items.Authors: T. E. Pickering, J. X. Prochaska, J. F. Hennawi, K. B. Westfall, D. Pelliccia, D. Reichwein, B. Holden, M. Brodheim, T. Ellsworth-Bowers, R. Cooke, F. Davies, F. Wang, M. Mandigo-Stoba
Items.Title: Current status of and future plans for PypeIt
Items.Abstract: PypeIt (pronounced "pipe it") is a Python package that enables semi-automated processing and data reduction of optical/near-IR spectroscopic data. PypeIt is designed to be a general purpose data reduction pipeline and currently supports ~50 spectrographs on ~18 telescopes.The algorithms within PypeIt build on decades of development on previous data reduction pipelines to produce robust science-grade data products.    With the release of version 2.0.0, PypeIt enters a more mature stage of development with a codified governance structure, a better defined software versioning system, and a more consistent release schedule. Efforts are ongoing to work more closely with facilities that PypeIt supports to improve its reliability and performance when handling data from those facilities. These efforts have been aided by an award from the NSF's Pathways to Enable Open-Source Ecosystems (POSE) program.

Items.Authors: Daniel Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Owain Snaith, Jyotirmay Paul, Sorabh Chhabra
Items.Title: Delay line actuator design and testing for the BIFROST instrument
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is a near-infrared (1 − 1.7μm) beam combiner and spectrograph that will be installed at the Very  Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) as part of the ASGARD array. To achieve fringes with an astronomi-  cal interferometer the beams of each telescope must be path length matched to below their coherence length.  BIFROST will rely primarily on the large delay lines of the VLTI and other instruments (HEIMDELLR), but  additional delay correction will be needed during operation. This small amount of delay correction (+-1 mm  minimum total distance) needs to be smooth and accurate (in the order of 50 nm steps) whilst being directly  implemented into the BIFROST servers. This paper will first discuss the delay actuator requirements needed  to achieve the science goals of BIFROST. The main body of the text will discuss each requirement and the  performance of the current actuator used and the future planned design.

Items.Authors: Tony J. Farrell, Nick Cerneaz, Sana Syed, Lewis G. Waller, Ross Zhelem, Satyam Mishra, Helen M. McGregor, Jahanzeb Zahoor, Mark Casali, Rolf Muller, Sambath Non, Slavko Mali, Urs Klauser, Vladimir Churilov, Yevgen Kripak, Zhemin Cai, David Roberston, Annino Vaccarella, Eckhart Spalding, Onur Şatır, Derya Öztürk Çetni, Gizay Yolalan, Ebru Uzunçam, Mehmet Kuruçolak
Items.Title: Delivery and acceptance testing of the DIRAC near infrared camera for the Türkiye National Observatories (DAG)
Items.Abstract: The DIRAC instrument (DAG InfraRed Adaptive optics Camera) has been built by Australian Astronomical Optics AAO (Macquarie University), Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics RSAA (Australian National University) and the University of Sydney (Australia) for the DAG400 telescope at the Türkiye National Observatories (DAG).    The DAG400 is a new 4-meter telescope with VIS/IR observation capability, located near Erzurum, Türkiye. A a focal plane instrumentation suite installed on a Nasmyth platform provides an AO optimized beam (TROIA), an adaptive stellar coronagraph (PLACID), and the DIRAC imaging camera. DIRAC provides a 30" FoV near-infrared diffraction limited camera for use with the AO optimized beam, and optionally with the coronagraph.     We examine the testing of DIRAC in Australia, and reassembly & successful commissioning on DAG400. Final on-sky end-to-end testing of DIRAC remains pending the full availability of the TROIA AO system, expected in 2026.

Items.Authors: Po-Hsuan Huang, Chun-Han Chou, Chih-Chung Yang, Po-Ming Lin, Pao-Chuan Tai, Chun-Chieh Lien
Items.Title: Design and development of a multi-spectral imager payload for PM2.5–PM1 aerosol monitoring on the FORMOSAT-8 mission
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present the multi-spectral imager design of a science-payload for air pollution monitoring, developed as part of the FORMOSAT-8D (FS-8D) program. These satellites will be placed in a sun-synchronous orbit. The first FORMOSAT-8 satellite already launched on 2025/11/29, and the science-payload will be installed on the fourth satellite (FS-8D). The payload is designed to monitor aerosol pollution in Taiwan, including PM1, PM2.5 and H2O. The science-payload consists of a VIS module and a SWIR module. The VIS module is designed to detect seven spectral bands for monitoring aerosol pollution. The SWIR module is designed to detect two spectral bands, enabling the identification of cirrus clouds and snow. Both modules have a swath greater than 200 km, enabling full aerosol data collection over Taiwan. The environmental validation of the optical payload is planned for completion in 2026, followed by the delivery of the flight model in 2027.

Items.Authors: Stephen P. Todd, Dan Dicken, Raziye Artan, Beth A. Biller, Cassandra Mercury, Katherine Morris, Vinooja Thurairethinam, Feng Zhao
Items.Title: Design and development of a near-IR integral field spectrograph for the HWO Coronagraph Instrument
Items.Abstract: The primary mission of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is to identify and characterise potentially habitable worlds. Spectra across a wide wavelength range are needed to cover multiple spectral features per molecule of interest. An integral field spectrometer (IFS), fed by a coronograph system, can be used to measure spectra from any planets within the nulled field of the coronograph, while also characterizing the residual speckles as a function of wavelength, enabling the contrast ratio to be further enhanced. We present design trades for an infrared IFS (0.8 to 1.7 µm) for the HWO Coronagraph Instrument, including assessment of the relative merits of lenslet and image slicer based architectures. Key requirements include full sampling of the speckle field at all wavelengths, maximized optical throughput, and control of spectral cross talk and stray light. We identify technology developments needed to advance the instrument design to the required technology readiness level.

Items.Authors: Ran Duan, Hanzhang Wang
Items.Title: Design and electromagnetic optimization of aluminum kinetic inductance detectors for 850 GHz astronomical observations
Items.Abstract: Targeting potential future 850 GHz ground-based facilities in China, we present the design of Aluminum LEKID arrays. Utilizing high-fidelity Sonnet simulations incorporating complex superconducting surface impedance, we optimized the pixel geometry on high-resistivity silicon. A key focus is mitigating electromagnetic crosstalk in high-density arrays required for these envisioned observatories. We rigorously investigate architectural solutions, specifically staggered pixel arrangements and inter-pixel ground shielding. Simulation results confirm significant isolation improvements. Future work will focus on fabrication and cryogenic characterization to experimentally validate the electromagnetic models. This work lays the technical groundwork for conceptual sub-millimeter instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Kemal Rüzgar, Gizay Yolalan, Burak Bülent Güçsav, Ebru Uzunçam, Cahit Yeşilyaprak, Deniz Becker
Items.Title: Design and test of simulator for Eastern Anatolia Observatory (DAG) telescope (DAGOS)
Items.Abstract: This study presents the design, laboratory validation, and full integration of the DAG Optical Simulator (DAGOS), a multi-wavelength and multi-field test platform developed for the 4 m DAG Telescope. DAGOS reproduces the F#14.2 beam, pupil geometry, and field coverage of the telescope through a reflective optical layout, adjustable multi-fiber sources spanning 630–2000 nm, and kinematic opto-mechanical mechanisms. Laboratory tests were performed upstream of TROIA, and the system is now ready for validation on the diffraction-limited DAG400 platform. DAGOS provides stable and repeatable illumination for coronagraphic mask testing, adaptive optics calibration, and the monitoring of non-common-path (NCP) aberrations. As a fully operational optical simulator, DAGOS supports both laboratory development activities and on-telescope verification processes.

Items.Authors: D. Dimitrova, R. D. Parsons, M. Kowalski, D. Berge
Items.Title: Design and verification of a simultaneous 4-channel CMOS system
Items.Abstract: Wide-field optical surveys such as LSST, ZTF, Pan-STARRS, and the upcoming ULTRASAT, are designed to periodically image large portions of the sky to detect and characterize transient objects. Each night, these surveys provide thousands of new sources making high cadence follow-up increasingly important. To address this, we have developed a cost-effective multi-channel optical follow-up system, using an off-the-shelf telescope and mount, commercial dichroic beamsplitters and components, enabling significant cost reduction through scaling. Initial observations show that the system is performing as expected, with depth limited by light-pollution rather than hardware. We have demonstrated that in proper observing conditions, the system can reach within 240s exposure time using a single telescope, the same limiting magnitudes as the ZTF. Multiple telescopes can be combined in an array to increase depth and surveying speed.

Items.Authors: Jian-Rong Gao, B. Mirzaei, M. Finkel, C. Walker
Items.Title: Design of a 2.7 THz dual-polarized quasi-optical HEB mixer
Items.Abstract: We design a 2.7-THz dual-polarized antenna in a novel configuration that feeds four hot-electron bolometers (HEBs) through coplanar-waveguide (CPW) transmission lines. The antenna performance is modeled using COMSOL Multiphysics, and its far-field beam pattern is analyzed when combined with an elliptical lens. The resulting dual-polarized, quasi-optical HEB mixer is suitable for supra-THz frequencies (>1 THz), as required for spaceborne heterodyne receivers to improve signal-to-noise ratio, and thus observing efficiency with minimal added complexity.

Items.Authors: Yuxin Qiu, Hanzhang Wang, Xiaoyun Ma, Ruirui Fan, Nannan Yue, Ran Duan
Items.Title: Design of a compact multilayer kinetic inductance detector for future infrared focal-plane arrays
Items.Abstract: Future infrared surveys require focal-plane arrays with high mapping speed and efficient spatial sampling. Compact pixels help approach Nyquist sampling of the point-spread function, reducing the need for dithering or complex scan reconstruction.  Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) can frequency-multiplex many pixels on a single readout line, making them well suited for large-format arrays. However, in conventional lumped-element KIDs, the interdigitated capacitor can occupy most of the pixel footprint — up to ~90% in reported designs — leaving only a limited active area for the radiation-absorbing inductor.  This work explores a compact multilayer KID for the 75~100 μm infrared band. The core concept is to move the capacitor below the absorber plane, reducing lateral capacitor occupation and allowing the top pixel area to be dominated by the radiation-sensitive inductor.

Items.Authors: Christopher T. Ratliff, Renate Kupke, Yuhui Wang, Phil Hinz, Matthew Radovan, Daren Dillon, Aaron Hunter, Brad Holden, Deno Stelter, Emily Plume, Javier Perez Soto, Nick MacDonald, Brian Peterson, Jerry Cabak, David Marques, Luke Gers, Marc Kassis, Adam Vandenberg
Items.Title: Design of a Hindle-Simpson metrology system for the Keck 1 Telescope adaptive secondary mirror
Items.Abstract: The Keck 1 Telescope will be retrofitted with a new adaptive secondary mirror. To calibrate the surface figure of this large (~1.45m) deformable aspheric convex secondary mirror we will use a Hindle-Simpson optical test. Typically the Hindle sphere optic must be larger than the convex aspheric mirror (1.68m in this case). For our design we will utilize a system that consists of sub-apertures to reduce expense and difficulties in manufacturing a full size Hindle sphere. In this paper we describe the mechanical and optical design of the Hindle sub-aperture array system (referred to as Hindle array henceforth), how we rotate it, adjust the sub-aperture cells, and stitch together the wavefront data. We will show results from a small scale prototype that has been assembled and tested and then present the mechanical subsystem designs for the full scale Hindle array.

Items.Authors: Boon-Kok Tan, Peter K. Day
Items.Title: Design of a kinetic-inductance impedance-matched parametric amplifier using an inverted microstrip architecture
Items.Abstract: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are key tools in superconducting quantum electronics but are inherently narrow band. While travelling-wave parametric amplifiers broaden bandwidth significantly, they require long nonlinear transmission lines or large junction arrays. An alternative approach, the impedance-matched parametric amplifier (IMPA), uses passive resonators to extend bandwidth, though most implementations rely on SQUID-based nonlinearity.    We present a kinetic-inductance IMPA (KIMPA) using niobium titanium nitride employing an inverted microstrip rather than a coplanar waveguide, reducing vulnerability to shorts, improving mechanical robustness, and enabling compact parallel-plate capacitors. Using a graph-based filter-synthesis model and harmonic-balance simulations, we predict a broadband gain profile demonstrating the viability of this architecture.

Items.Authors: D. Vaccaro, K. Nagayoshi, V. Anvekar, M. D. Audley, P. Barry, C. Bellucci, M. Bruijn, T. Ghigna, J. W. A. den Herder, P. Hargrave, K. Karatsu, J. van der Kuur, L. Lamagna, A. Pascual Laguna, S. Oguri, A. Paiella, F. Piacentini, G. Signorelli, A. Tartari
Items.Title: Design of a sensor-readout chain based on antenna-coupled TES bolometers and FDM readout for future space CMB instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Detecting primordial B-modes in the CMB polarization requires unprecedented sensitivity and systematic control. Antenna-coupled TES bolometers with Frequency-Domain Multiplexing (FDM) readout are a leading technology for future space CMB missions, offering high sensitivity, broad multiplexing, and cryogenic compatibility. Building on heritage from missions such as NewAthena and SPICA, this work presents the first European development of this detector chain for CMB polarimetry, supported by ESA.  We report on the preliminary design of a full on-chip sensor-readout chain targeting the 90–150 GHz band, covering dichroic dual-polarization TES bolometers and FDM cold readout components. The TES detectors use a TiAu bilayer on a suspended SiN membrane; the RF circuitry, designed via SONNET and HFSS simulations, is based on NbTiN on a-SiC:H. The FDM architecture features high-Q LC filters and a two-stage SQUID optimized for space. Planning for fabrication and test phases is also outlined.

Items.Authors: Xiaolan Huang, Shibo Shu, Miao Li, Sunil R. Golwala, Feng Liu
Items.Title: Design of a six-band, 2.4-octave (80-420 GHz) hierarchically summed phased-array slot-dipole antenna array for NEW-MUSIC
Items.Abstract: The Next-generation Extended Wavelength Multi-band Sub/millimeter Inductance Camera (NEW-MUSIC) is the first six-band trans-millimeter wave polarimeter mounted on the Leighton Chajnantor Telescope (LCT). To realize this innovative instrument, we propose a broadband, hierarchical phased-array antenna integrated with band-defining filters, covering a wide spectral range of 80~420 GHz (2.4 octaves)[1]. This design enables key scientific investigations, including studies of trans-millimeter emission from time-domain sources, hot plasmas in galaxy clusters and galaxies via the Sunyaev-Zeldovich effects, and dusty sources spanning from galactic star-forming regions to high-redshift star-forming galaxies. The integrated antenna-filter system provides a critical technical foundation for NEW-MUSIC’s high-performance detection capabilities.  [1] Huang X et al. Design of a Six-band, 2.4-Octave (80--420 GHz) Hierarchically Summed Phased-Array Slot-Dipole Antenna Array for NEW-MUSIC,arXiv:2511.08990

Items.Authors: Devika K. Divakar, Joseph Strubhar, Andrew Pinckney, Phillip MacQueen
Items.Title: Design of an atmospheric dispersion corrector and double scrambler for improved fiber coupling and illumination uniformity for the HET HRS
Items.Abstract: High-precision radial velocity programs with the HET-HRS rely on exceptionally stable fiber illumination. We present the design of a new fiber-feed module integrating a static Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector and a Double Scrambler. The ADC, optimized for the HET's unique fixed-zenith-angle range, employs fixed Amici prisms to achieve chromatic correction, ensuring maximum coupling efficiency into the fiber core across the 360 - 1000 nm spectral band. We detail the optical prescription of ADC and mechanical integration within the Prime Focus Instrument Package. We also present the optical and mechanical concepts of Double Scrambler mechanism, which is a critical subsystem for minimizing the radial velocity noise by decoupling variations in input illumination from the spectrograph's output point spread function, significantly stabilizing the instrument. These two subsystems are essential for maintaining HET-HRS's stability, enabling long-term high-precision radial velocity measurements.

Items.Authors: Xianke Song, Jiahao Zhou, Yingfu Wang, Wengfei Liu, Kai Yun, Mengmeng Qian, Haoyang Zhang, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Design of an autofocus system for a long-distance fiber view camera
Items.Abstract: To ensure the positioning accuracy of optical fibers in the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), this study addresses focal plane deviation caused by large temperature variations in the Fiber View Camera (FVC). An autofocus system is developed, integrating an external focusing mechanism with a software algorithm that combines image clarity evaluation and hill-climbing search. The system achieves a 100% focusing success rate, effectively replaces manual focusing, and maintains both fiber positioning precision and telescope observation efficiency.

Items.Authors: Xin Luo, Shao-Zhen Zhu, Yu Ning, Bao-Long Chen, Wei Liu, Zhe Geng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of operational software for infrared test system
Items.Abstract: The MCT Infrared Test System serves as a critical platform for driving and controlling infrared detectors, as well as for data acquisition and performance characterization; its stable operation depends on a reliable software system. In this paper we describe the design and implementation of a comprehensive software system tailored to the operational control and detector performance test requirements of the MCT infrared test system. In the system we employ a layered architecture consisting of an SDK and a client layer. The SDK layer encapsulates core functional interfaces such as device connection, parameter configuration, and exposure control, while the client layer, built on the Qt framework, provides a graphical user interface supporting parameter settings, image preview, FITS file saving and playback, and status monitoring. Additionally, the system offers excellent compatibility and can support detector arrays of various specifications, including 640×512 and 1k×1k.

Items.Authors: Lei Wang, Jiahao Dong, Hangxin Ji, Songxin Dai
Items.Title: Design of slit-mask for the imaging spectrometer (OASIS) of the 10-meter-class optical and infrared telescope
Items.Abstract: Design of a Slit Mask for the Imaging Spectrometer (OASIS) of a 10-Meter-Class Optical and Infrared Telescope    The Optical Astronomical Spectrograph & Imaging Subsystem (OASIS) is a first-light instrument for a 10-meter-class optical/infrared telescope, supporting multi-target spectroscopy and imaging over a 9′×3′ field of view.    The slit mask consists of thin plates distributed on a spherical surface to match the telescope focal plane, covering ~600 mm × 200 mm and accommodating hundreds of slits with customizable positions and geometries.    This work analyzes slit mask design requirements, including panel forming and slit position/shape accuracy under different observing conditions. Key factors affecting performance are evaluated, and corresponding design and fabrication strategies are proposed.

Items.Authors: Arun Surya
Items.Title: Design of the calibration system for MOIS: a multi object imaging infrared spectrograph
Items.Abstract: MOIS is a multi-object configurable slit spectrograph designed to be used with the 3.6 Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). It will cover the near-infrared wavelength band of 0.97 - 2.37 microns and have a spectroscopic field of view of 9’ x 3’ arc minutes. We describe the design of the calibration system for MOIS. With the large focal plane area covered by the configurable slit units, a calibration system should provide the focal plane with the same beam configuration and also match the exit port of the integrating sphere with the exit pupil of the telescope. Considering the 80 mm focal plane surface trade studies are made to understand if a scanning mode flat fielding and wavelength calibration beam would be optimal. We describe the optical design of the calibration system together with the design trades made to achieve uniformity requirements.

Items.Authors: Meng Zhai, Qian Chen, Wei Wang, Boqian Xu
Items.Title: Detectability of water vapor on terrestrial exoplanets around GK stars with Tianlin
Items.Abstract: China has proposed a space telescope with aperture size of 6.6 meters named Tianlin, which is dedicated for the characterization of rocky planets in the habitable zones (HZ) around nearby GK stars. It will be equipped with a low to high resolution spectrograph and a high contrast coronagraph that should allow the delivery of high quality spectrum of exoplanets. We conduct a preliminary simulation of transmission and reflected spectra for Earth-like planets around G, K type stars and perform retrieval analysis of the detectablity of H2O, a key bio-indicating molecule. Our results show that Tianlin has the ability to constrain H2O abundances in the atmosphere of Earth-like planets in most cases.

Items.Authors: Roser Juanola-Parramon, Christopher Stark, Corey Spohn, Alex Howe, Neil Zimmerman, Sarah Peacock, Noah Tuchow, Susan Redmond, Bryony Nickson
Items.Title: Determining the astrophysical noise floor of the Habitable Worlds Observatory’s coronagraphs
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory will use a coronagraph to block starlight and reveal faint, potentially Earth-like planets around nearby stars, and to spectrally characterize them in search of oxygen, requiring SNR > 10. Achieving this science goal demands suppressing and subtracting residual starlight to a few parts in 10¹².  The challenge is often framed primarily in terms of telescope and instrument stability, the dominant engineering driver for HWO. However, many coronagraphs capable of 10⁻¹⁰ raw contrast are sensitive to details of the astrophysical scene (stellar angular diameter, hot exozodiacal dust, and starspots), which can introduce residual structure in the PSF potentially limiting starlight subtraction to levels above the required few parts in 10¹² and imposing an astrophysical, rather than instrumental, noise floor.  Here we present estimates of this astrophysical noise floor with the baselined HWO coronagraphs (AAVC and APLC) and evaluate ADI.

Items.Authors: Shibo Shu, Daikang Yan, Yaqiong Li, Jiamin Sun, Lin Zhu, Ye Chai, Zhouhui Liu, He Gao, Zhengwei Li, Xufang Li, Wenhao Wu, Congzhan Liu
Items.Title: Development of 6-inch detector modules for AliCPT1
Items.Abstract: AliCPT1 is a dedicated CMB polarization telescope at the northern hemisphere. The working temperature is around 300mK. The focal plane is built for 19 6-inch detector modules. In our design, each detector module has 456 pixels. We have developed both silicon-plated and metal horn arrays for this work. The beam symmetry is better than 90% and the cross-polarization is below -20dB. The TES detector array uses Al-AlMn in series. The current DRIE yield is better than 96%. To study the uniformity of the TES transition temperatures, 120 sensors have been measured. The microwave SQUID multiplexers are under development. The packaging of all components has been massively tested. Details will be presented in this talk.

Items.Authors: Yuxin Qiu, Hanzhang Wang, Ran Duan, Xiaoyun Ma, Ruirui Fan, Nannan Yue, Xiaojing Wu, Wei Duan, Fei Liu, Gang Xu
Items.Title: Development of a 5000-pixel kinetic inductance detector array for far-infrared imaging
Items.Abstract: The development of a 5000-pixel superconducting Aluminum Kinetic Inductance Detector (KID) imaging array for far-infrared astronomy (350 μm) is presented. The array features a large-scale frequency division multiplexing readout architecture with 1,000 resonators per feedline. Characterization at 50 mK demonstrates a fabrication yield greater than 95%, with intrinsic quality factors exceeding 200,000. Design strategies to minimize frequency crosstalk are discussed, alongside the resulting trade-offs in multiplexing ratios and filling factors. Future plans include the integration of feedhorn arrays and room-temperature readout electronics to establish a complete detection instrument for observational experiments.

Items.Authors: Jee-Ho Kim, Boon-Kok Tan
Items.Title: Development of a compact sideband-separating SIS mixer for the Africa Millimetre Telescope targeting 211-373 GHz
Items.Abstract: Many millimeter and sub-millimeter astronomical observatories require separating signals from different frequency sidebands to avoid spectral confusion. Traditional receivers accomplish this using waveguide components–hybrids, power splitters, directional couplers–and a set of double-sideband (DSB) superconducting mixers. At higher frequencies, however, these components become bulky, difficult to manufacture, and add loss.    We present a new compact architecture replacing most waveguide elements with modular superconducting planar-circuit chips. By re-arranging the DSB mixers and integrating waveguide components directly on-chip, we achieve full sideband separation while substantially reducing volume and complexity. We demonstrate this approach for the ALMA band 6+7 frequency range for the Africa Millimetre Telescope’s first-light instrument and outline its scalability to adjacent bands. Our design takes a promising step toward large multi-pixel receiver arrays for future telescopes.

Items.Authors: Jae-Hyuck Choi, Hagyong Kihm
Items.Title: Development of a deep ultraviolet Fizeau interferometer for the homogeneity evaluation of UV telescope optical materials
Items.Abstract: Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) is a critical optical material for UV space telescopes such as NASA's GALEX, serving in transmission grisms, and imaging windows owing to its high transmission down to 193 nm. Optical material’s homogeneity is conventionally evaluated using Fizeau interferometry at 633 nm; because the refractive index of CaF2 increases toward shorter wavelengths, inhomogeneities negligible in the visible can become significant at operational ultraviolet wavelengths. This study presents an in-house developed deep-ultraviolet (DUV) Fizeau interferometer for at-wavelength evaluation of CaF2 at 193 nm. Single-crystal CaF2 samples grown by the Czochralski method were measured at both 193 nm and 633 nm, and the wavefront errors were used to derive the spatial refractive index distribution. The results show that the measured homogeneity differs significantly between the two wavelengths, indicating that conventional 633 nm interferometry may fail to detect inhomogeneities at UVs.

Items.Authors: Wouter van Straalen, Johannes Algera, Niels Ligterink, Pierre Piron, Jérôme Loicq
Items.Title: Development of a goniometric spectro-polarimeter for planetary surface analogue measurements
Items.Abstract: In the study of planetary bodies, spectrometry of reflected light is widely used to characterize the composition of planetary surfaces. However, the light polarization, which can be studied in addition to the spectrum, also carries information about the microscopic structure of planetary surfaces. The reflected polarization can be connected to the grain size, porosity, birefringence, crystal structure, signatures of living organisms, and more. To expand our knowledge on the possible applications of spectro-polarimetry in planetary surface characterization, the AgSPARROW (A goniometric Spectro-PolARimeteR for Optical and NIR Wavelengths) instrument is being developed at TU Delft to measure the spectro-polarimetric signature of light reflected from planetary surface analogue samples at various phase angles. The study will focus on investigating polarization signatures that can reveal additional information about surface structures which is inaccessible with only spectral measurements.

Items.Authors: Shigeyuki Sako, Keito Kurashima, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Yuki Hirao, Emon Kodama, Hideto Yoshida, Taketo Ando, Daisuke Takada, Kosuke Kushibiki, Mamoru Doi, Koji S. Kawabata, Tomonori Totani, Keiichi Maeda, Masaomi Tanaka, Yuu Niino, Ryota Fukai, Ryou Ohsawa, Satoshi Takita, Jin Beniyama, Taiga Sasaoka, Sorato Wada, Shodai Nezu, Haruka Nagasawa, Natsu Madokoro, Yosuke Takamura, Yuzuru Yoshii, Takashi Miyata, Kotaro Kohno, Kentaro Motohara, Takeo Minezaki, Fumi Egusa, Itsuki Sakon, Masahiro Konishi, Takafumi Kamizuka, Hidenori Takahashi, Kana Morokuma-Matsui, Hiroaki Sameshima, Mitsuyoshi Yamagishi, Masataka Imai, Takashi Horiuchi, Natsuko M. Kato
Items.Title: Development of Laguna: an optical instrument complex for the TAO 6.5-m telescope
Items.Abstract: Laguna is an optical instrument complex under development for the TAO 6.5-m telescope. Designed for both general observations and time-domain astronomy, Laguna integrates multiple observational units within a common mechanical structure sharing the telescope focal plane. Three units are currently being developed: Laguna-CAM, Laguna-SPEC, and Laguna-SPAD. Laguna-CAM is a simultaneous three-band CMOS imaging unit with a 4-arcmin-diameter field of view (FoV), providing efficient multi-band observations and color information during high-speed observations. Laguna-SPEC combines a low-dispersion NUV prism spectrograph and a medium-dispersion echelle spectrograph, providing spectroscopic coverage from 300 to 1000 nm. Its slits are permanently located within the Laguna-CAM FoV, enabling rapid spectroscopic follow-up without changing observing modes. Laguna-SPAD is a high-speed imaging and polarimetric unit employing a large-format SPAD image sensor for sub-second and millisecond observations.

Items.Authors: Yuan Liang, Jiajia Wu, Jianan Cong, Kai Zhang, Zijian Han, Zhengyang Li, Tong Zhou
Items.Title: Development of the Cassegrain focus instrument for the 1-meter telescope of Wuhan University
Items.Abstract: A Cassegrain focus instrument is developed for the 1-meter Telescope of Wuhan University. It is composed of a wide-field photometric camera and a low-resolution spectrograph to support the astronomy team at Wuhan University to study formation and evolution of galaxies, star clusters and other objects. The wide-field photometric camera can achieve image quality with FWHM ≤ 1” over a field of view of 0.44°× 0.32°. The low-resolution spectrograph has a long slit of 8’ to observe extended sources like galaxy. It can select desired spectral resolution R=1000,1500, 3000 by switching slits and cover a wide wavelength range of 400–900 nm by rotating a grism wheel. In August 2025, the instrument successfully got its first light on the Wuhan University’s 1-meter Telescope at the Lenghu astronomical site. With the commissioning observations, the instrumental performance has been further optimized and met the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Poli, Andrea Orlati, Marco Morsiani, Veronica Baldini, Igor Coretti
Items.Title: Development of the digital servo system for enhanced pointing accuracy of the 32m Gavril Grueff VLBI antenna in Medicina
Items.Abstract: High frequency observations rely critically on the stability and accuracy of a radiotelescope pointing mechanism. To establish operational autonomy and achieve higher technical performance, we initiated the independent development of a new servo system for the 32-m Grueff Antenna. Our study prioritized an empirical characterization of the telescope’s dynamics. We developed a custom drive interface allowing for high-fidelity in-situ testing. Experimental data acquired through this process highlighted critical design requirements for the system upgrade. Results demonstrate that a robust active anti-backlash torque sharing strategy is paramount to mitigate mechanical play. Furthermore, the analysis confirmed that optimal tracking precision requires strict load-to-motor inertia matching and the adoption of ultra-low cogging motors to minimize velocity ripples. Finally, the observed non-linear behaviors dictate the implementation of adaptive control architectures, such as gain scheduling.

Items.Authors: Ken Miyato, Atsushi Nishimura, Rin Yamada, Chieko Miyazawa, Toshikazu Takahashi, Sho Masui, Yasumasa Yamasaki, Hideo Ogawa, Toshikazu Onishi, Takeshi Sakai, Nami Sakai, Kazuki Tokuda, Ken'ichi Tatematsu
Items.Title: Development of the new 7-beam wide-band (72-116GHz) receiver 7BEE for the Nobeyama 45m telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the development and commissioning of the new 7-beam wide-band (72–116 GHz) receiver 7BEE installed on the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. The receiver enables highly efficient observations in the 70 GHz band for studies of the earliest phases of star formation. In addition, it provides observations with approximately 1.4--3.2 times higher observation efficiency than that of the FOREST receiver over the common frequency range of 80-116 GHz.   The system incorporates wide-band corrugated horns and cryogenic LNAs and newly designed optical and RF components. In the 70 GHz band, the receiver noise temperature is typically 80 K in laboratory measurements, while the system noise temperature is typically 250 K under typical observing conditions at Nobeyama. During commissioning and science verification observations, we confirmed that the receiver satisfies the observatory requirements, and it is now available for scientific observations.
